::api-operation{method="POST" path="/v1/businesses/{biz}/payments/{pay}/refund"}
#docs
A payment on an invoice is refunded as revenue (contra-revenue, capped by what that invoice's credit notes do not already claim). A payment on NO invoice is held as the customer's excess credit — it is refunded out of that credit instead, capped by the payment's `remaining_minor` in `GET …/customers/{cus}/excess_payments` (invoices draw the excess balance oldest payment first) and by the customer's current excess balance. A refund above that cap is refused with a 400. A payment that is neither is refused with a 400. That list's `refundable_minor` is what is refundable this way.

## Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `biz` | `string` | **yes** | Business id (biz_…) |
| `pay` | `string` | **yes** | Payment id (pay_…) |

## Headers

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | `string` | no | Safely retry writes — repeats return the original response. If a write FAILED after it had already taken effect, that failure is what repeats: the key is spent, and a new attempt needs a new key. |

## Body

The request body is optional.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount_minor` | `integer` | no | Omit for the full remaining amount. |
| `reason` | `string` | no | Why the refund is made. |
| `confirm_repeat` | `boolean` | no | Set to true to send a refund that repeats one sent in the last 10 minutes (same payment, same amount). Without it, the repeat is refused with a 409 `possible_duplicate`. |
| `on_decline` | `string` | no | What happens when the gateway declines this refund after it accepted it, for this refund only. `block`: the money stays with the business. `issue_credit`: the customer gets it as refundable credit on an open credit note. Stored on the refund, so a decline that arrives later by webhook uses it. Omitted: the business rule (`billing_rules_config.declined_refund`). Applies to a refund of an invoice payment; a refund of held excess credit always returns to that credit. One of `block`, `issue_credit`. |

## Response

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `object` | `string` | The object type. |
| `id` | `string` | The refund's id (re_…). |
| `payment` | `string` | The id of the payment that is refunded. |
| `status` | `string` | The refund's status. One of `succeeded`, `pending`, `failed`. |
| `amount_minor` | `integer` | The refund amount in minor units. |
| `currency` | `string` | The refund's currency (ISO-4217 code). |
| `reason` | `string` | Why the refund was made. |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `201` | Created |
| `400` | Not refundable / over-refund |
| `404` | No such payment |
| `409` | Possible repeat: this payment already has a pending or succeeded refund of the same amount from the last 10 minutes (`error.code` is `possible_duplicate`). Nothing is booked. Send the request again with `confirm_repeat: true` to send the refund anyway. |

#request
```bash [Request]
curl -X POST "$TMBILLING_URL/v1/businesses/biz_XXXXXXXXXXXX01/payments/pay_XXXXXXXXXXXX01/refund" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TMBILLING_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "amount_minor": 2900
  }'
```
